title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: declarative agents read images embedded in Word, PowerPoint and PDF files
summary: Hold: whole-agent blocking is not the only documented agent-level control. The briefing also overlooks Microsoft's general rollout guidance and its explicit statement that embedded knowledge files are used only as text for grounding.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated this feature's default state or whether administrators must enable it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, embedded file content bullet; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether image reading applies to embedded file content is not stated.
claims.quote: Embedded knowledge agents support uploading files as knowledge sources. Copilot only uses the text content of these files for grounding.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whether image reading applies to embedded file content is not stated' with 'Microsoft’s agent-details page says embedded knowledge agents use only the text content of uploaded files for grounding; the image-understanding release note does not reconcile that limitation.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-details#manage-agents-with-embedded-file-content-as-a-knowledge-source. Narrow the knowledge-source open question to the remaining undocumented coverage rather than treating embedded-file behaviour as wholly unstated.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and the release-notes entry describe no identity or permission change.
claims.quote: Searched: identity and permissions in the roadmap description and the full release-notes passage for 531758. Both describe image-based grounding and examples; neither describes an identity or permission change.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes grounding answers, not actions taken on a user's behalf.
claims.quote: By combining textual and visual understanding, Declarative Agents deliver more comprehensive and contextually accurate responses for complex queries.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking applies to the whole selected agent and prevents every user in the organisation from using it.
claims.quote: Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Microsoft Copilot and other host products.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry agents affects only their availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The only agent-level lever is the whole-agent block.
claims.quote: When you delete an agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the agent is soft deleted. A soft-deleted agent is unavailable to its maker and end users
claims.fix: Replace 'No setting for image reading is documented, so the only agent-level lever is the whole-agent block (see the controls table), which stops the agent for every user' with 'No setting specifically for image reading is documented; the whole-agent block shown in the controls table stops the agent for every user.' Do not claim that blocking exhausts the documented agent-level controls.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits SharePoint site content in organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discovery, not existing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use, such as summarising an open document.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery needs a Microsoft Copilot licence and the SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available. See Prerequisites for SharePoint Advanced Management.

claims.claim: User access is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access offers All users, No users and Specific users or groups.
claims.quote:
The setting has three options:
All users
No users
Specific users or groups

claims.claim: All users is the documented default for User access.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: User access controls who can use agents and plugins, rather than what those agents read.
claims.quote: Use User access to control how members of your organization access and install agents and plugins.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated any rollout mechanics.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft has not stated the default or any rollout mechanics' with 'Microsoft has not stated this feature’s default. The release-notes page describes a general safe deployment model that gradually expands from a subset of users within a tenant to the organisation.' Keep the feature-specific default as unknown.

claims.claim: When an agent uses SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge, Copilot searches files, folders or sites accessible to the user.
claims.quote: When you configure your agent to use SharePoint and OneDrive content as knowledge, Copilot searches SharePoint and OneDrive files, folders, or sites that a user has access to for grounding information.
